title: Advance Durable Goods Orders (Sep 2026 data)
source: CENSUS: census.gov/manufacturing/m3/release_schedule.html grid decodes to 'September 2026 | 10/27/2026' (advance report; full report 11/3/2026) and census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html carries 'Advance Report on Durable Goods--Manufacturers' Shipments, Inventories, and Orders | October 27, 2026 | 8:30 AM | September 2026' (id A202610270830) — both fetched direct 2026-09-04 and promoted estimate -> confirmed by this event's own initial research, the condition the no-self-confirm limit names
notes: THE FUNDING RISK THIS ROW WAS FILED FOR IS RETIRED; WHAT SURVIVES IS THE ADDRESS. The initial research (2026-09-04) closed the delay branch on a primary: H.R. 6500, the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act 2027, was SIGNED 2026-09-02 (whitehouse.gov) funding through 2026-12-11, after the House cleared the Senate text 370-48 on 2026-09-01 — firing the 09-25 ledger's 'CR signed on or before 2026-09-30' kill switch 28 days early. The risk migrated rather than vanished, to durable-goods-2026-12-23, which sits 12 days past the CR's expiry. What still earns this row: the release lands 08:30 on DAY 1 of the Oct 27-28 FOMC (federalreserve.gov calendar, fetched 2026-09-04), at the front of the Oct 27-29 compound window — consumer confidence 10:00 and MSFT AMC the same day, GOOG/META plus the 14:00 statement on 10-28, AMZN/AAPL plus the Q3 GDP advance and PCE on 10-29. That address makes it LESS tradeable, not more: across 16 FOMC day-1 sessions the intraday range runs ~17% (SPY, median 0.723% vs a 0.876% two-year median, p36) / ~19% (QQQ, 0.998% vs 1.235%, p33) narrower than ordinary, while the overnight gap is statistically ordinary (SPY 8/16 above median, exactly the null) — and the same method recovers the known decision-day signature correctly signed (gap p26, range p69). No durable-goods release in the measured 12-release sample has ever landed on an FOMC day-1, so 10-27 is the first observation of this configuration. Reading order is unchanged from the predecessor — ex-transportation first, nondefense capital-goods shipments second, headline last (sigma 3.74 vs 0.34) — and NOT an AI-capex read, since new and unfilled orders exclude semiconductor manufacturing by construction; MSFT's own print that evening is the better capex signal. One channel is tighter here than for the 09-25 edition: September is the third month of Q3, so the shipments line prints two days before the 10-29 GDP advance. Researched in docs/research/events/durable-goods-2026-10-27.md.
